problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport aircraft. Available containers are:

* Container 1: weight 13 tons, revenue $271,000
* Container 2: weight 42 tons, revenue $212,000
* Container 3: weight 27 tons, revenue $171,000
* Container 4: weight 7 tons, revenue $61,000
* Container 5: weight 42 tons, revenue $133,000
* Container 6: weight 21 tons, revenue $52,000
* Container 7: weight 41 tons, revenue $101,000
* Container 8: weight 12 tons, revenue $282,000
* Container 9: weight 16 tons, revenue $258,000
* Container 10: weight 34 tons, revenue $57,000
* Container 11: weight 28 tons, revenue $299,000
* Container 12: weight 33 tons, revenue $128,000
* Container 13: weight 33 tons, revenue $181,000
* Container 14: weight 18 tons, revenue $273,000
* Container 15: weight 25 tons, revenue $237,000
* Container 16: weight 7 tons, revenue $299,000
* Container 17: weight 1 ton, revenue $219,000
* Container 18: weight 6 tons, revenue $186,000
* Container 19: weight 19 tons, revenue $289,000
* Container 20: weight 48 tons, revenue $39,000
* Container 21: weight 4 tons, revenue $200,000
* Container 22: weight 12 tons, revenue $60,000
* Container 23: weight 16 tons, revenue $193,000
* Container 24: weight 34 tons, revenue $27,000
* Container 25: weight 49 tons, revenue $179,000
* Container 26: weight 36 tons, revenue $130,000
* Container 27: weight 37 tons, revenue $124,000
* Container 28: weight 21 tons, revenue $55,000
* Container 29: weight 44 tons, revenue $51,000
* Container 30: weight 4 tons, revenue $60,000

The aircraft has a maximum payload capacity of 510 tons. Choose the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this weight limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
